scale_statement.quote: The Council evaluates its identified risks on a five-point scale on the likelihood or probability of the risk occurring (rated between rare and certain) and the impact caused should the risk occur (rated between negligible and critical).

evaluation_levels.definition: likelihood and impact without additional, specific mitigation action
evaluation_levels.quote: Gross level – likelihood and impact without additional, specific mitigation action.

evaluation_levels.definition: current likelihood and impact, based on mitigation action already put in place but excluding further mitigation action planned
evaluation_levels.quote: Actual level - this is the current likelihood and impact, based on mitigation action already put in place but excluding further mitigation action planned.

evaluation_levels.definition: future level of likelihood and impact based on any additional mitigation action (if any) planned
evaluation_levels.quote: Expected level – this is a future level of likelihood and impact based on any additional mitigation action (if any) planned to further address the triggers and the consequences of risks.

combination.rule: risk score = likelihood score x impact score, range 1-25; every printed cell score in Figure 1 equals the product of its row (impact) and column (likelihood) scores. The strategy does not state the multiplication in words.
combination.axes: rows = Impact (1 Negligible ... 5 Critical); columns = Likelihood (1 Rare ... 5 Certain)

figure_quote.quote: The Council has chosen to divide the rating into bands as shown on the risk matrix below, defining the criteria used to manage the risk exposure and reflecting the risk appetite levels described above.

combination.consistency_note: Each matrix cell label falls in the Table 4 score band of the same name (Low up to 3, Moderate 4-6, High 8-12 [Table 4: 'Medium - High'], Extreme 15-25); no cell score is printed outside a band.

descriptor.quote: The Council aims to operate with a financial risk between £250k – £500k.

The Council aims to operate with a legal risk that finely balanced between flexible and open, following approved standards and practices as far as possible but also allowing for innovation, willing to engage in new areas of work, of significant public interest, and related to high value transactions.

cells.Averse: Following approved standards and practices, engaging in business as usual, low value transactions
cells.Cautious: Following approved standards and practices, engaging in business as usual, increased value transactions
cells.Flexible: Following approved standards and practices as far as possible, innovating, public interest, high value transactions
cells.Open: Innovating, new area of work, significant public interest, high value transaction

table_row.quote: Following approved standards and practices as far as possible, innovating, public interest, high value transactions Innovating, new area of work, significant public interest, high value transaction

descriptor.quote: The Council’s reputation is one of the most important assets which employees and Councillors aim to protect to ensure there is little chance of significant repercussions.

descriptor_2.quote: the Council is seeking an open reputational risk, with possible significant reputational damage or enhancement.

cells.Averse: No chance of any repercussions / negative comments
cells.Cautious: Little chance of significant repercussions and mitigation in place beforehand
cells.Flexible: Exposure of greater scrutiny and public interest. Management through listening and active engagement. Risk of reputational damage.
cells.Open: Experimental– possible significant reputational damage or enhancement
cells.Seeking: Unprecedented – probable significant reputational damage or enhancement

table_row.quote: Experimental– possible significant reputational damage or enhancement Unprecedented – probable significant reputational damage or enhancement

descriptor.quote: The Council aims to operate with an open appetite for innovation and for crafting service delivery models and initiatives that redefine the ways in which residents and stakeholders are enabled to achieve their outcomes.

cells.Averse: Essential development of core business only
cells.Cautious: Maintain status quo; new schemes are tried and tested only by others
cells.Flexible: Encourage innovation through new schemes offered to the Council
cells.Open: Proactive pursuit of innovation and crafting solutions that have not been attempted before
cells.Seeking: Desire to ‘break the mould’ and challenge current working practices

table_row.quote: Proactive pursuit of innovation and crafting solutions that have not been attempted before
